author: val
body: Every wanted value here is taken from the mathematics, never from a run of DeviceMath, so a body that drifts cannot drag its own expectation along with it. A row reads ok when the answer is within tolerance and prints what it got when it is not, which keeps the expected file stable against a change in how a Real is shown.

author: val
body: Four rows are controls that no defect in the scaling, the quadrant fold or the series can move: sqrt 0.25, sqrt 1.0, sqrt 4.0 and sin 0.0 were all exact on 2026-07-28 while sqrt 1e6 was answering 15646 for 1000 and sin 3.0 was thirty-five per cent wrong. Verified by sabotage the same day: restoring the old bodies turns twenty-six rows red and leaves those four green, so a wholesale red is distinguishable from the rows that carry the assertion. Do not delete them to shorten the test.

author: val
body: sin squared plus cos squared is the one assertion here that does not depend on a constant typed into this chapter, so it holds even if every wanted value above were mistyped. Under the old bodies it read 0.9886 at 1.7 radians and 0.9877 at 3.0.
